title: Object design

1.label: below
1.name: Below the bar
1.meaning: Concerning for this level; this alone would likely block an offer.

2.label: developing
2.name: Developing
2.meaning: Some signal, but clear gaps for this level.

3.label: meets_bar
3.name: Meets the bar
3.meaning: What a solid candidate at the chosen level shows.

4.label: above_bar
4.name: Above the bar
4.meaning: Would read as the next level up.

level_bar.junior: A reasonable set of classes with mostly clear responsibilities and one flow that works.
level_bar.mid: Bounded requirements, one job per class, correct relationships, two flows that walk, an extension that fits.
level_bar.senior: All of mid, plus clear abstractions, state and concurrency handled where they matter, and a stated trade-off with the rejected alternative.
level_bar.staff: All of senior, plus testability, clean seams for future change, and pushing back on scope with reasons.

competencies.name: Requirements and use cases
competencies.looks_for: Actors, main use cases, and what is out of scope.

descriptors.2: Partial use cases; scope keeps growing or stays vague.
descriptors.3: Bounded requirements with actors and main use cases.
descriptors.4: Prioritises use cases and says what is out of scope and why.

competencies.name: Class model
competencies.looks_for: Domain classes with one responsibility each and correct relationships.

descriptors.1: God classes or unclear ownership of state.
descriptors.2: Reasonable nouns but mixed responsibilities or wrong relationship kinds.
descriptors.3: One responsibility per class; correct uses, has-a, is-a and implements choices.
descriptors.4: Clean abstractions; composition over inheritance where behaviour varies, with a reason.

competencies.name: Behaviour and code
competencies.looks_for: Main flows walked method by method; pseudo code matches the diagram; state transitions and concurrency.

descriptors.1: Cannot walk a flow through the classes.
descriptors.2: Flows walk with gaps, or the code calls methods the model does not have.
descriptors.3: Two main flows walk correctly in pseudo code that matches the model.
descriptors.4: Handles state transitions and concurrent access cleanly.

competencies.name: Extensibility and trade-offs
competencies.looks_for: How the model absorbs the extension; patterns used for a stated reason; alternatives considered.

descriptors.2: The extension needs edits across many classes or a growing chain of conditionals.
descriptors.3: The extension fits with few edits; a pattern is used for a stated reason.
descriptors.4: Names alternatives and why they were rejected; considers testability.

scoring_notes: Do not judge UML notation or naming style.
Distributed system concerns earn no credit here unless the problem asked for them.
Red flags are only the items in red_flags. Weak, wrong or incomplete answers lower the matching competency score and are never red flags.
red_flags: Makes up facts and keeps defending them after being questioned
Hostile, insulting or disrespectful toward the interviewer
Refuses to engage with the questions
Integrity issue, such as reading answers from another source or getting outside help during the round
